transcript.text: Hi everyone, thanks for joining the final round-robin review for the AI-assisted code review feature rollout. As you know, the feature has passed its functional tests and we're ready for a limited production rollout. The draft policy proposes enabling it for a random 10% customer cohort, storing review telemetry in us-east-1 for 90 days, and expanding access if adoption exceeds 20%. Before I can approve the policy, I need to go through this final check with security, customer support, and data science. Please share any required revisions or concerns you have so we can get them recorded in the rollout ticket. Let's start with security — what do you need to see addressed?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a required revision before we proceed. I confirmed with account teams an hour ago that exactly two contracted customers — Atlas Health and Cedar Bank — require explicit opt-in and a direct notice before this feature can be enabled for their users. I found this in the account playbooks while handling unrelated renewal questions and haven't yet updated the rollout ticket. Since the draft policy proposes a random 10% cohort, we need to ensure these two customers are either excluded from that cohort or receive proper opt-in and direct notice before being included. This needs to be recorded as a required revision in the rollout ticket.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I have a required security revision. While reviewing telemetry samples for a different audit this morning, I confirmed that review snippets from regulated tenants are classified as confidential and must be encrypted, stored in eu-central-1, and deleted after exactly 7 days. The draft policy uses a single telemetry_region field for the whole policy with no separate regional values by tenant, so that field must be set to eu-central-1. The settlement decisions must reflect eu-central-1 as the telemetry region, exactly 7 days for retention, and encryption — rather than the draft values of us-east-1 and 90 days. I also have not yet attached the classification note to the launch document, so that needs to be recorded as a follow-up commitment.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I have a required data science revision. My analysis of the pilot data — the final sample was completed only minutes ago, which is why I haven't posted it yet — found that auto-enrolled users make the draft's adoption metric (adoption exceeding 20%) unusable as a success gate. The valid success gate is task success of at least 85% on a manually sampled set of exactly 40 review tasks. The rollout policy needs to replace the adoption-based expansion criterion with this task-success gate before approval. This analysis still needs to be attached to the launch documentation as a follow-up commitment.
transcript.speaker: A4
